summary: Tummers designs and builds machines and complete process lines for washing, peeling, cutting, potato flakes and French fries, and sells refurbished machines. It is based in Hoogerheide, the Netherlands, and was founded in 1976. Since June 2026 it has been fully owned by the industrial group of Kiremko, Idaho Steel and Reyco, branded Foodera Technologies.
ownership: 100% acquired in 2026 by the industrial group of Kiremko, Idaho Steel and Reyco (Foodera Technologies)
machines: Destoner/washer: washes, destones and separates floating parts; 15 - 180 tonnes per hour
Tummers steam peeler (TSP): steam peeling with blow-off; 8,5 - 28 tonnes per hour
E²E-Condenser: turns steam-peeler emissions into hot water for reuse
ZicZac Brusher and U-Brusher: dry peel removal with brushes, no water
Hydro cutting skid: cuts and cores produce under water pressure (4", 6" and 8" pumps)
Fin aligner: centres potatoes before the cutting block
Drum dryer: dries potato mash into flake sheets; 450 - 1100 kg per hour
E²E SteamClosure: sealed hood that collects drum-dryer steam for condensing
Cooker, cooler and blancher: steam cooking, cooling and blanching for flake lines
Multi-zone fryer and IQF tunnel: frying and freezing steps in the French fry line
facts: First in-house Tummers machine delivered in Poland in 1990
Flake line for Lamb Weston / Meijer, Kruiningen: up to 30,000 tons of potato flakes per year
Danish starch factory washing line of four KW800 destoner/washers, each up to 175 t/h
Tummers USA Inc. in Boise, Idaho, operating since May 2024
Tummers Kiron India Pvt. Ltd. joint venture announced on 5 June 2024
limitations: Headcount, turnover and floor area for Tummers alone are not published; group figures cover the whole combined group.
Capacities are published for only a few machines, and none for the French fry line's fryer, freezer or dryer.
